title: Audit Logs & Admin Activity Review with Nova Capital
summary: Redwood security + SE walkthrough of audit log capabilities and admin activity logging. Covered what events are captured, retention options, export integrations (S3, syslog, Splunk), KMS/HSM for log encryption, SOC2/ISO references, and next steps to provide reports and run a short export test. Customer concerned about retention, export latency, and proof of non-repudiation for admin actions.
action_items: Alex Chen: Share SOC 2 Type II report, audit-log schema, and sample JSONL export (due 2025-08-22)
Priya Patel: Schedule follow-up demo to show live export to Nova's S3 bucket and run a retention policy change (due 2025-08-27)
Sofia Vega (Nova): Provide test S3 bucket ARN and a list of SID/roles to test export permissions (due 2025-08-25)
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC2 + ISO/27001 docs and audit log schema
Set up a 30-minute demo to stream audit logs to Nova's S3 and validate fields
Run a one-week retention experiment and share export artifacts (JSONL)
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2025-08-20 15:00 UTC
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Rachel Lin (Nova CISO), Mark Duarte (Nova DevOps), Sofia Vega (Nova Sec Eng)

Summary (auto): quick security review focused on Audit logs and admin activity; agreed to exchange SOC2 docs and run an S3 export test.

[00:00] Alex (Redwood): hi everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros?
[00:08] Rachel (Nova): hey, i'm rachel, ciso at nova, i'll be primary for compliance questions.
[00:12] Mark (Nova): mark, devops, i'll own the export/infra side.
[00:16] Sofia (Nova): sofia, security eng, i'll look at the log contents and retention.
[00:20] Alex (Redwood): great. priya and i will run through how our audit logs capture admin activity, exports, retention controls, and KMS integration.
[00:30] Priya (Redwood): quick note, i'll demo screenshots and schema. audio might have slight transcribe quirks, apologies if names come out weird.

[02:05] Alex (Redwood): first high-level, we capture all admin-actor events: console logins, SSO assertions, token/key management (API key create/revoke), role changes, permission grants, and any config changes to deployment/route rules. also system alerts like failed logins and suspicious IPs.
[02:22] Mark (Nova): do you log API keys usage or just creation/revocation?
[02:30] Priya (Redwood): both. we record key lifecycle events and also API access events tied to token IDs for non-repudiation. there is a request_id and session id per call so you can correlate tokens to requests. sometimes the token id name is transcribed as tkn-id in our schema.

[05:10] Rachel (Nova): for SOC2 evidence we'll need immutable records and proof that logs haven't been tampered with. how do you handle tamper-resistance?
[05:20] Priya (Redwood): logs are write-once in our internal store, we maintain append-only sequences, and exports are signed. we can integrate with customer KMS so exported files are encrypted with your key. for stronger non-repudiation you can push logs to your S3 bucket or to Splunk/Datadog via syslog or HTTP, so your own retention and immutability controls apply.
[05:45] Sofia (Nova): is there an option for streaming to our SIEM? low-latency?
[05:52] Alex (Redwood): yes, two modes: near-real-time streaming via syslog/HTTP (typically sub-30s delivery under normal load) or batch exports (hourly/daily) as gzipped JSONL. streaming uses TLS and mTLS if you want client certs.

[08:12] Mark (Nova): format of logs? we prefer JSON lines with specific fields.
[08:18] Priya (Redwood): primary export format is JSONL with fields: timestamp, event_type, actor_id, actor_role, resource, action, request_id, session_id, ip, user_agent, region, raw_payload. for console actions we include a delta of the config change. i'll attach the schema. sometimes transcription spells it JSON-L, etc.

[11:30] Rachel (Nova): retention - we have regulatory needs for 7 years for some logs, others 1 year. what are your retention limits?
[11:40] Alex (Redwood): hosted customers get configurable retention tiers: 30 days (default), 90 days, 365 days, and custom retention for enterprises (e.g., multi-year) under dedicated/private agreements. long-term retention can be exported automatically to your bucket for cold storage.
[12:05] Sofia (Nova): can retention be per-tenant or per-log-type? we only need admin activity kept longer than low-level access logs.
[12:12] Priya (Redwood): yes, retention is configurable by route and by event_type; you can pin admin_activity to retain for longer while normal inference logs are shorter. we'll show policy examples in the follow-up.

[15:00] Mark (Nova): are sensitive fields redacted? e.g., user prompts, user PII?
[15:08] Priya (Redwood): for prompts or payloads we support redaction and pseudonymization at export time; the internal audit store keeps a hashed reference and metadata but you can opt-in to remove raw payloads from exported logs. encryption at rest is default and exports are encrypted in transit with TLS.

[18:22] Rachel (Nova): KMS details - can we use our AWS KMS / CloudHSM?
[18:28] Alex (Redwood): yes, we support customer-managed keys in AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and HSM integrations for private deployments. when configured, exported objects are encrypted with your CMK and we do not retain plaintext keys. some small transcribe typo earlier noted KSM but meant KMS.

[20:45] Sofia (Nova): what about admin console actions - who changed RBAC, who created service accounts?
[20:52] Priya (Redwood): every RBAC change is logged with before/after state, the actor, IP, and timestamp. we also capture SSO assertions (SAML/OIDC) with assertion id and session metadata. for on-prem or VPC installs we can forward audit logs to your internal SIEM without leaving the VPC.

[24:10] Mark (Nova): export destinations - you mentioned S3, Splunk, Datadog, syslog. any support for BigQuery or Azure Blob?
[24:20] Alex (Redwood): yes, we support S3, Azure Blob Storage, GCS, direct ingestion to Splunk/Datadog via HTTP HEC, syslog forwarders, and BigQuery exports via GCS->BQ pattern. we'll provide a step-by-step for each.

[27:00] Rachel (Nova): auditability for privileged users - can you provide an audit trail we can link to our internal ticketing?
[27:10] Priya (Redwood): we provide a correlation id that you can pass back into your ticket, and we can optionally attach the log snippet to a ticket via webhook. also we support a read-only audit viewer role so auditors can see logs without admin privileges.

[30:30] Sofia (Nova): are logs searchable? retention queries?
[30:36] Alex (Redwood): yes, in the console you can query events by time range, actor, action, and request_id. for heavy search needs we recommend streaming to Splunk/Datadog or BigQuery. console queries are optimized for recent data; archived exports are better for deep historical analysis.

[33:50] Mark (Nova): timing for exports - if we stream to S3, how soon will files arrive?
[33:56] Priya (Redwood): streaming is near real-time; if using batch export the default is hourly. files are rotated per hour and named with the hour window and sequence id. we'll share filename convention in the schema doc.

[36:40] Rachel (Nova): are deletion and retention policies auditable? we need to show when something was deleted and by whom.
[36:48] Priya (Redwood): deletions are themselves logged as admin events (who triggered deletion, what was deleted, and when). for compliance we can produce an evidence package showing retention changes and delete events.

[39:05] Alex (Redwood): to recap next steps: we'll send SOC2 + ISO docs, audit-log schema and a sample JSONL, and schedule a short follow-up to stream logs to your S3. priya will run the demo and sofia will provide a test S3 ARN.
[39:22] Rachel (Nova): sounds good. also can you include any SLA around log delivery?
[39:30] Alex (Redwood): yes, for Dedicated we can SLA delivery and durability; for hosted we publish typical delivery windows and best-effort streaming SLAs - i'll include those in the doc pack.

[41:00] Mark (Nova): one last question, retention costs and long-term storage pricing?
[41:06] Alex (Redwood): long-term retention is usually via export to your storage which you pay for; we charge for extra replication and retention if you want Redwood to store multi-year archives. i'll include example pricing tiers.

[43:10] Rachel (Nova): ok thanks everyone.
[43:14] Sofia (Nova): thanks.
[43:20] Alex (Redwood): thanks all — action items we'll email and set up follow up.

References/shared artifacts:
- SOC2 Type II (link provided by Alex)
- Audit log schema (attached by Priya)
- Sample JSONL export (will be sent)

End of transcript.
